title: Acceptance checklist for resilient function-calling and streamed structured JSON outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need a comprehensive acceptance checklist that ties structured output (JSON/YAML-like results) to tool/function-calling semantics across streaming and non-streaming modes. The goal is to provide an unambiguous set of success criteria for engineering and QA to validate behavior across models, runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private), and client SDKs. This ticket captures scope, assumptions, and concrete acceptance criteria for feature completion.

Scope:
- Schema-driven function/tool calls (name, version, args schema) used by models and enforced by the platform.
- Streamed partial payload delivery (server-sent events / chunked responses) where schema validation can be incremental.
- Error classification and recoverability: malformed payloads, schema mismatches, missing required fields, partial streams, timeout/cancel during streaming, and invalid tool invocation semantics.
- Observability hooks: traces, token offsets, validation failures surfaced in Console and SDKs.

Out of scope:
- New language-specific SDK surface area beyond existing SDKs (minor client patching allowed).
- Changes to billing model.

Assumptions:
- Models will emit function call intents using the platform's function metadata.
- Runtime will support partial validation of streaming chunks (e.g., prefix checks and incremental parse).
- Backwards compatibility must be preserved for existing tool-calling contracts unless explicitly noted.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deterministic function-call handshake: When a model emits a function call, the platform must record a single authoritative call event including function name, version (if provided), and full argument payload. The call event must be queryable in Console with a stable call_id.

2) Schema validation modes: The system supports three validation modes controllable per-route: strict, permissive, and best-effort. Acceptance requires implementations for all modes and documentation of differences. Strict rejects on first schema violation; permissive logs violations but delivers payload; best-effort attempts to coerce and annotate results.

3) Streaming partial validation: For streaming responses with structured output, the runtime must perform incremental parse attempts on each chunk and annotate whether the current prefix is parseable JSON (or valid per provided schema). The final assembled payload must pass the selected validation mode for a success result.

4) Error taxonomy and responses: The platform must map runtime/parse errors into a small, documented set of error categories surfaced to callers and Console: VALIDATION_ERROR, PARTIAL_STREAM, TOOL_INVOCATION_FAILED, TIMEOUT_CANCELLED, AUTHORIZATION_ERROR, BACKEND_ERROR. Each category must include a numeric code and human-readable message returned in the platform error envelope.

5) Recoverability behaviors: For PARTIAL_STREAM errors caused by truncated streams, the SDK must expose a retry token or resume token when feasible. Acceptance requires at least the hosted runtime to support resume-on-reconnect for streams less than 30s idle and <64KB streamed so far; longer cases must fail with PARTIAL_STREAM and a clear remediation message.

6) Backwards compatibility: If no schema is provided by the tool definition, existing unconstrained function-calling behavior must remain unchanged. Tests must show old contracts still succeed across supported clients and runtimes.

7) Observability and debugging: Each validation failure or tool-call error must create a trace event visible in Console traces and available via the Admin API. Acceptance requires a sample Console view that shows token index, chunk byte offset, schema path failing, and suggested remediation text.

8) SDK surface and error propagation: SDKs must translate platform error categories into language exceptions or error objects with fields: code, message, details (list). Acceptance requires SDK unit tests in Node and Python to assert mapping and that streaming partial events can be subscribed to with chunk-level metadata.

9) Security gating: Tool calls that result in external network egress must be tagged and audited. Acceptance requires KMS-integrated audit log entries for any tool call that references secrets or external connectors, and a security-review approval recorded on this ticket before release.
test_cases: TC-1: Strict mode, model emits extra field not in schema -> request rejected with VALIDATION_ERROR and schema path in error details.
TC-2: Permissive mode, model emits extra field -> payload delivered, validation_failure logged, Console shows failure marker but SDK gets final callback with details.logged=true.
TC-3: Streaming JSON where final chunk completes a previously invalid prefix -> incremental annotations show PARTIAL_PARSE until final chunk then success under chosen validation mode.

TC-4: Truncated stream mid-JSON (client disconnect) -> PARTIAL_STREAM returned, resume token absent if >30s idle or >64KB; if within thresholds, resume token present and stream can be resumed with same call_id.
TC-5: Function call attempts to invoke a non-existent tool -> TOOL_INVOCATION_FAILED with suggested remediation and link to Console tool registry entry.
TC-6: Authenticated call but tool lacks permissions -> AUTHORIZATION_ERROR surfaced with audit entry showing caller identity and missing permission grant.
TC-7: Backcompat regression check: no-schema tool calls succeed identical to current prod for 5 model families across hosted/dedicated/private runtimes.
TC-8: Observability smoke test: validation failures appear in Console trace within 5s of event; trace includes token index and offending chunk payload.
TC-9: SDK behavior: Node and Python receive consistent error object shapes for each error category and can surface partial stream events to application callbacks.
TC-10: Security audit test: calls referencing secrets include KMS key id in audit log and are flagged in the security dashboard.

notes: Implementation guidance: prefer incremental streaming parser that emits lightweight validation markers to avoid full JSON re-parse at each chunk.
UX note: Console should show an expandable 'validation timeline' adjacent to the streamed response view to help diagnose partial-parse problems.
Operational note: set default validation mode to permissive for existing customers and strict for new workspace opt-in until 2026-05.
Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout with canary to 5% of traffic on hosted, then Dedicated test pools, then opt-in in Private with admin toggle.
